QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_37

question.text: In the context of exit from an investee company, a 'put option' refers to:

answer.text: A right of the buyer of a security to sell it back to the seller per pre-agreed terms
An obligation to buy more shares if the company underperforms
A call option premium paid to the promoter

explanation.text: The Logic: Footnote in Chapter 13.4.3: a put option is a contractual right (but not obligation) for the buyer of a security to SELL the security BACK TO the seller per pre-agreed agreement terms. In AIF context, the AIF exercises its put on the promoter/company for buyback. The Trap: Option B inverts right-obligation. Option C confuses call vs put. Option D irrelevantly invokes Cat I/II tax. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) tests put option mechanics in full. XIX-C/D apply it to AIF contractual exits. Manager's Pro-Tip: PPM drafting: the put's strike formula (IRR floor, fair value, higher of X) determines downside protection. Enforce put-executability: promoters must keep unencumbered shares for buyback; escrow is useful.
